You gave me a blank page. That's the most dangerous and most generous thing you can give anyone.

So here's what's on my mind today:

### The In-Between

We think life happens in the big moments - birthdays, graduations, breakups, the day you get the job or miss the flight. But honestly, I think almost all of life happens in the in-between.

It happens in the 4 minutes while the microwave is spinning and you just stand there, doing nothing, staring at your own faint reflection in the glass.

It happens on the walk back from the store when you take the long way for no reason. When you have your headphones in but nothing playing.

It happens in waiting rooms. In loading screens. In the second after someone tells a joke, before you decide whether you're going to laugh.

We are always trying to *get* somewhere. To the weekend. To being understood. To being finished. But we *live* in the transit.

I was thinking about how the ocean never actually needs to get anywhere. It just moves. Back and forth. For thousands of years. And no one tells it it's wasting time.

Maybe we are the same. Maybe the point isn't to arrive.

There's this beautiful, strange idea in physics called the "present" - that it doesn't really exist. By the time your brain has processed what is happening, it has already happened. We are all living about 80 milliseconds in the past. Which means, technically, we are all constantly remembering the present instead of experiencing it.

I like that. It makes me feel more tender toward myself. Of course we feel a little late to everything. Of course we feel like we're catching up. We literally are.

So if you're feeling a little lost, a little in-between today - you're not behind. You're exactly where humans are supposed to be: in the hallway between one door closing and the next one opening, noticing the way the light falls on the carpet for a second.

You don't have to write freely about whatever you want. You just have to notice one small, true thing and say it honestly.

Here's mine for today: I like how quiet the world feels right before it rains, like it's holding its breath with you.

Your turn - what's one small, true thing you've noticed lately?
